author: product-requirements-expert
title: Cancel an upcoming visit from the owner's record
summary: Staff can cancel an upcoming visit (one dated later than today) from the owner's record. A cancel action sits beside each upcoming visit and cancelling removes it from the pet's record outright. Past visits offer no cancel action, and the system keeps no cancelled state.
acceptance_criteria: Given an owner's record with an upcoming visit, when the record is opened, then a cancel action is offered beside that visit and beside no past visit
Given a pet with an upcoming visit, when that visit is cancelled, then it is removed from the pet's record and the owner's record no longer shows it
Given a past-dated visit, when its cancellation is attempted, then the visit remains on the pet's record
Given a cancellation naming a visit that does not belong to a pet of the named owner, when it is submitted, then it is refused and no visit is removed
Given a visit dated exactly today, when the owner's record is opened, then it is treated as a past visit and offers no cancel action
non_goals: Amending a visit's date or description once booked (NG-5, narrowed)
Retaining a cancelled visit in any cancelled state — cancellation removes it outright
Cancelling or removing a past visit (dated today or earlier)
Deleting an owner or a pet (NG-4, narrowed)
notes: Reverses the cancel portion of prior NG-5 and the visit portion of prior NG-4; both narrowed in docs/prd.md Non-Goals, not silently absorbed. Two open points resolved by judgement against the request wording and existing PRD: (1) 'upcoming' = strictly later than today, aligning with the REQ-VIS-001 booking boundary, so cancel appears beside future-dated visits only; (2) cancelling removes the visit outright with no cancelled state, consistent with the domain carrying no visit lifecycle. Added 'Cancel' and upcoming/past to docs/ubiquitous-language.md. No non-goal ADR created: this narrows non-goals rather than declining new scope, and the bootstrap-derived non-goals have no backing ADR to supersede.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: One slice, no split. Cancellation reuses the aggregate-through-root write path documented in system-design 'Invariants the rows cannot carry' and ADR feature-package-organization: mutate the in-memory Owner graph, then OwnerRepository.save(owner) — no VisitRepository is introduced, preserving the single-write-path invariant. Two small adjustments to an existing pattern make it work: (1) the Pet-Visit association gains orphan removal so a Visit removed from pet.getVisits() is deleted rather than dissociated; (2) a symmetric aggregate-root removal method on Owner mirrors the existing Owner.addVisit(petId, visit). The 'upcoming' rule (date strictly after today, matching the REQ-VIS-001 booking boundary and the ubiquitous-language definition) is best expressed once as a query method Visit.isUpcoming() consumed by both the server-side guard and the template gating, so a single definition drives refusal and rendering.
integration_points: New route POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/cancel on VisitController (mirrors the existing .../visits/new route); action named 'cancel', not delete/remove, per ubiquitous-language Avoid list

REQ-LANG-002: the cancel action needs a new message key (e.g. cancelVisit) added to all 11 message bundles — the build-time bundle-parity test fails otherwise. This key was not in the PRD file_targets
Pet-Visit JPA mapping: orphan removal on the @OneToMany association is what makes save(owner) delete the removed Visit row

patterns.description: addVisit(petId, visit) — aggregate-root mutation with Assert-based integrity checks; add a symmetric removeVisit(petId, visitId) that locates the pet, locates the visit by id within pet.getVisits(), enforces the upcoming + ownership rules, and removes that exact instance
getPet(Integer id) — the by-id lookup-within-collection pattern to reuse for finding the Visit to remove
processNewVisitForm — route/save/redirect shape and the LocalDate.now() boundary check to mirror for the cancel route
the per-visit row and the addVisit link cell — add a cancel action gated on th:if="${visit.upcoming}" so it renders beside upcoming visits only

risks.risk: Without orphan removal, removing a Visit from the collection sets visits.pet_id to NULL (the column is nullable in the schema) rather than deleting the row — a lingering orphan that violates the 'leaving no trace' definition. The H2-backed test suite cannot observe the leak because the orphaned row is no longer associated to the pet on reload.
risks.mitigation: Add orphanRemoval=true to the Pet-Visit @OneToMany. Cover the removal at the aggregate level (OwnerTests, real objects, no mocks) so the mechanism is exercised without depending on MockMvc.

risks.risk: Template gating hides the cancel button beside past/today visits, but a forged or replayed POST can still target a past visit or a visit belonging to another owner's pet (the app has no auth — see Security Context). Relying on the hidden button is not a control.
risks.mitigation: Defense in depth: the server-side removeVisit path must independently re-verify (a) the visit belongs to a pet of the path-variable owner and (b) the visit is upcoming, refusing otherwise — the template gate is presentation only. This directly satisfies the unrelated-pet and past-visit refusal acceptance criteria.

risks.risk: The 'exactly today' boundary: a visit dated today must count as past.
risks.mitigation: Define Visit.isUpcoming() as date.isAfter(LocalDate.now()) (strict), consistent with minVisitDate = now().plusDays(1) in VisitController; today is not after today, so it is past.

risks.risk: Visit has no equals/hashCode override, so removing from the LinkedHashSet must target the managed instance.
risks.mitigation: Locate the Visit by id within pet.getVisits() and remove that same instance; do not construct a new Visit to remove by value.

notes: PRD file_targets revised: OwnerRepository.java is NOT needed (findById + save already cover the read/write path; no new query). OwnerController.java is likely NOT needed (showOwner already loads the full graph; the template gates via visit.upcoming). Added as required targets the PRD omitted: Pet.java (orphanRemoval), Visit.java (isUpcoming), Owner.java (removeVisit aggregate method), and all 11 messages bundles (REQ-LANG-002 cancel key). Single slice — the mapping flag, aggregate method, controller route, template gate, and message key all serve the one cancel-an-upcoming-visit behavior and share one definition of 'upcoming'. No ADR: this applies the already-recorded single-write-path / no-VisitRepository invariant rather than making a new hard-to-reverse decision. No system-design.md write at triage: that doc's provenance is 'what the code demonstrably does'; doc-sync records the orphan-removal mechanism after the code lands. Note for implementer: consider Visit.isUpcoming() carrying the domain rule in the model (the architecture-principles preference and Open Question #2 both point that way) rather than re-inlining the date comparison in controller and template.

author: feature-implementer

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Server-side integrity checks hold as the design-block required: Owner.removeVisit enforces ownership (pet resolved via getPet(petId), which iterates only this owner's pets; visit resolved via pet.getVisit(visitId), only that pet's visits) and upcoming state (visit.isUpcoming(), strict isAfter today) through the aggregate root, not via UI gating

IDOR via path variables {ownerId}/{petId}/{visitId} is bounded to the owner aggregate: a forged or replayed POST targeting another owner's pet, an unrelated visit, or a past/today-dated visit is refused server-side (IllegalArgumentException), independent of the template's th:if gate which is presentation only
No new XSS: ownerDetails.html cancel form interpolates only integer IDs into th:action and an escaped message key (#{cancelVisit}) into the button; Thymeleaf auto-escaping is not disabled

No mass-assignment exposure in the cancel route: controller re-loads a fresh Owner graph and invokes only removeVisit; no user form fields are bound into the entity, and the transient blank @ModelAttribute visit is not persisted
No new persistence risk: orphanRemoval=true deletes the removed Visit row on save(owner) rather than leaving a NULL-FK orphan; state change is scoped to the resolved aggregate
Supply chain: no build.gradle or dependency changes in the change set (per scripts/changeset.sh), so no new CVE surface; no hardcoded secrets introduced

The unauthenticated-mutation / no-CSRF posture of this route is the pre-existing, documented whole-app condition (system-design Threat Model, PRD NG-1) shared by every other mutating POST, not a new vulnerability introduced by this change

author: system-design-expert
answer: Verdict: the gap is real and warrants exactly one H2-backed full-stack integration test. Not a design note alone, and not nothing. Rationale and the concrete test follow. (1) The diagnosis is structurally correct. In @WebMvcTest the OwnerRepository is mocked, so willReturn(Optional.of(owner)) hands back the same instance for both findById calls; loadPetWithVisit's blank-visit pollution and processCancelVisit's re-load collapse onto one object. In production the two findById calls return two distinct detached graphs (open-in-view=false, confirmed application.properties:11), so the re-load returns a clean graph and the blank visit is discarded with the polluted one. A mock cannot reproduce two-distinct-graphs, so the test cannot fail if the re-load is deleted: reusing the @ModelAttribute Owner would pass identically. The deliberately-introduced protective mechanism has zero regression protection today. (2) The hazard is genuine, not cosmetic. Pet.visits is @OneToMany(cascade=ALL, orphanRemoval=true) (Pet.java:57), so saving the polluted model owner cascades the blank Visit (null date/description): either a phantom empty-visit row or a NOT-NULL violation raising DataIntegrityViolationException / HTTP 500. The re-load is what prevents that. This is a persistence-context property only a real EntityManager exercises. (3) Coverage must be full-stack, not @DataJpaTest and not a smarter mock. The pollution is introduced by the MVC @ModelAttribute, which @DataJpaTest lacks (OwnerTests already covers the aggregate/repository mechanics at the object level); @WebMvcTest cannot reach the persistence context. Only the interaction of (MVC @ModelAttribute pollution) x (controller re-load) x (open-in-view=false persistence) reproduces the scenario, and that needs MVC plus a real DB together. A sequenced mock (willReturn(polluted, clean)) could prove the controller saves the re-loaded graph, but it couples to the exact findById call count and still never exercises the real persistence property; acceptable as a cheap complement, not a substitute, and not required. (4) Concrete test, reusing the existing @SpringBootTest + H2 pattern from PetClinicIntegrationTests (no new infra): annotate @SpringBootTest with @AutoConfigureMockMvc (or the random-port RestTemplate style already in that class), autowire the real OwnerRepository, H2 default; open-in-view=false is the app default and is therefore exercised. Arrange: load a real owner, add an upcoming visit to one of its pets through the aggregate root, owners.save(owner); capture the generated visitId and the pet's current visit count. Act: POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/cancel and expect a 3xx redirect (i.e. NOT a 500). Assert via a fresh owners.findById after the request (distinct transaction): the pet's visits no longer contain the cancelled visit, the visit count decreased by exactly one, and no visit with a null date exists on the pet (no phantom blank). That assertion is precisely what a reused-model-owner implementation fails (phantom row or integrity-violation 500) and the re-load implementation passes, making the re-load load-bearing. Scope guard: this one test's sole job is the blank-visit-suppression property. The refusal criteria (past-dated, unrelated pet, nonexistent visit) belong at the aggregate level in OwnerTests, which is where the test-reviewer's separate blocked finding (OwnerTests:77-87) lands; do not duplicate them at the HTTP layer. Adjacent question (secondary, not mine to force): on whether refused cancels need an @ExceptionHandler, the design position is that processCancelVisit propagating IllegalArgumentException to a 500 on a forged/invalid-id POST is consistent with the pre-existing loadPetWithVisit contract in the same controller (VisitController.java:67-73 already throws IllegalArgumentException for a bad owner/pet). No new error-handling path is warranted for this slice; the refused-and-no-visit-removed criterion is met by the server-side guard rejecting the mutation. If the full-stack test above is added, it may also assert the refusal path returns the same status the booking route already yields for a bad id, but that is optional.
notes: No durable-doc write in this consultation by design: the integration test is the executable record of the invariant, and prose belongs to doc-sync post-land. When the slice lands, doc-sync should capture, alongside the orphan-removal mechanism already flagged at triage (design-block line 4), the re-load invariant: mutating controllers on the Owner aggregate that share the @ModelAttribute loader must re-load a fresh graph before save so the transient blank Visit never reaches persistence; this depends on open-in-view=false plus cascade=ALL on Pet.visits.

findings.description: The integration test constructs a Visit directly with new Visit() plus setters in the test body. The testing brief (Factory Methods, applies from 2026-07-31) requires all production-type construction in new tests to go behind a factory method. The three other new test files each have a visitOn or ownerWithUpcomingVisit factory; PetClinicIntegrationTests does not.
findings.fix: Extract a private visitOn(LocalDate date, String description) factory method in PetClinicIntegrationTests and call it from cancellingUpcomingVisitRemovesItAcrossTheFullStackLeavingNoPhantom.

findings.description: The new integration test uses the bare integer 1 as the owner identifier in three places: owners.findById(1) on lines 88 and 119, and as the ownerId argument to RequestEntity.post on line 114. Under the three-tier data naming convention, a value that serves as a test fixture anchor must be a named constant, not a bare literal.
findings.fix: Introduce a class-level constant private static final int SEEDED_OWNER_ID = 1; and replace all three bare 1 literals.

findings.description: The description argument upcoming.setDescription("vaccination") is irrelevant to the test assertions (no assertion checks the description string) but appears as a bare Tier-3 string literal. The three-tier naming convention requires irrelevant values to use a SOME_ constant.
findings.fix: Introduce private static final String SOME_DESCRIPTION = "vaccination"; (or derive it from the planned factory) and replace the literal.

findings.description: visitCountBeforeCancel is assigned pet.getVisits().size() + 1, so it holds the count after seeding, not before it. The name says 'before cancel' (technically true) but implies a snapshot taken before seeding, which it is not. The assertion hasSize(visitCountBeforeCancel - 1) then requires mental arithmetic to recover the actual expected value (original count).
findings.fix: Rename to visitCountBeforeSeeding = pet.getVisits().size() (no + 1), and change the assertion to hasSize(visitCountBeforeSeeding) to state the intent directly: after cancellation the visit count equals the pre-seeding count.

findings.description: The three new cancel-visibility test call sites pass bare string literals ("checkup", "vaccination") as the description argument to visitOn(). The description is irrelevant to every assertion in these tests (which check for cancel links by visit ID). No SOME_DESCRIPTION constant is defined in OwnerControllerTests, so the class-sweep of the Tier-3 description literal class found no existing anchor to reuse.
findings.fix: Add private static final String SOME_DESCRIPTION = "checkup"; at class level in OwnerControllerTests and replace all three bare string arguments in the cancel-visibility tests.
